newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan October export orders up 4.35 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan October export orders up 4.35 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Foreign orders for Taiwan goods rose 4.35 percent in October from October 1995 to US$10.295 billion, the third highest monthly total on record, the economics ministry said on Wednesday.
The following is a table of export data in millions of U.S. dollars.
The ministry attributed October's rise mainly to rising foreign demand for computer and information products.
Overall orders from the United States rose 7.92 percent to $3.04 billion, with information and telecommunication products accounting for $660 million of the total.
Orders from Hong Kong decreased a year-on-year 2.86 percent to $1.87 billion, while orders from Japan were down 5.95 percent to $1.28 billion.

European orders jumped 17.56 percent to $1.71 billion, hitting an all-time monthly record high. The rise also was due to strong demand for information and telecommunication products, which accounted for $130 million of total orders from Europe.
Orders in Taiwan's key information and telecommunications sector increased 15.52 percent to $1.62 billion, while orders for lower-tech electronics fell 11.56 percent to $1.35 billion.
Textile orders were down 3.02 percent to $1.28 billion and base metal products orders down 2.02 percent to $826 million.
Machinery orders grew a scant 0.3 percent to $669 million.
Plastics and rubber products orders were down 3.71 percent to $597 million.
Orders for transportation tools and equipment grew 5.12 percent to $472 million.
